style.vernacular: Najd plateau capital laid out on a grid of 2 km blocks: flat-roofed 1-3 storey villas behind walls in beige, sand and cream painted render or stone cladding, mid-rise slab blocks, and a cluster of glass towers on the northern axis; historic Najdi mud-brick buildings with crenellated parapets and small triangular window openings survive at Diriyah and the Masmak; public buildings favour desert-beige limestone, travertine or precast panels. Ground is sand and paving with date palms and acacia in planted verges.
style.ornament: Najdi triangular and rectangular window openings (furjat) in patterned rows, stepped crenellated parapets (shurfat) with inverted triangles beneath, projecting peepholes (tarma), carved wooden doors, palm-trunk columns, plain exteriors with decoration inside; modern Saudi civic buildings use giant geometric cut-outs and arcades.

sources.what: mud-brick Najd style, furjat triangular openings, shurfat crenellated parapets, tarma peepholes, courtyards, mosques mostly without domes
adobe walled town; later marble with a desert-beige tone; 2x2 km grid; Kingdom Centre, Burj Rafal, Faisaliah; hot desert climate

local limestone cladding, triangular windows, arcades and stepped parapets
